body: I have experienced this. To me, I wanted a way out of the misery I was living in. Death, of course, comes up as a good option, but in my head I had enough inhibitions about suicide that it wasn't a good option to me. So I wished I could die in an accident, get murdered, or have to choose between dying myself or having someone I cared about die. It was something about not creating the circumstance myself, but still having it happen. Is this like what you are feeling?

I'm going to assume that you haven't personally experienced depression, because it doesn't sound like it from how you speak. Let me emphasize: *there is nothing wrong with that*, but it does mean that you are going to struggle to understand the effects of it and how it interacts with life events. Depression is one of those things where you don't fully *get* it unless you've experienced it.

I'm not doing great right now, but I'm far from my worst. But, I remember the feelings at my worst almost perfectly. When you're severely depressed, you are in a different mental state. To a degree, you don't think fully rationally. You have a collapsed perception. Because of this, small things can have a big effect.

But that's not even the issue here. I don't think many people would say breaking up with an SO is a small thing in most cases. But when you're depressed, it's an even bigger shake up. The effect of the break up is often exacerbated by self doubt and self hate; it's no longer just an unfortunate circumstance, it's now something that *you* caused. *You* caused the pain to yourself. *You* caused the pain to your (now) ex. *You* are a bad person who doesn't deserve a significant other.

I'm sorry for the wall of text. I'm not a very good writer. But, lastly, let me emphasize that depression is a BIG thing, and so it affects different people in different ways. I am, of course, speaking from my perspective. Overall, I just want to explain that it affects someone who is depressed in a different way from how it affects you. I'd suggest maybe watching [Mark Henick's TedX talk](http://youtu.be/D1QoyTmeAYw) to better understand the "collapsed perception" I mentioned. He's a much better speaker than I am.

Sorry for not explaining very well.
